(1) the interpretability of a CNN’s hidden representations depends on the training method, (2) the interpretability improves with training iterations and is higher in networks trained with a larger batch size, and (3) the interpretability is higher in the deeper layers of the network.

(i) interpretability is a useful axis of comparison between CNN models and training techniques, (ii) the interpretability of CNN models improves with training iterations, (iii) the interpretability is affected by the initialization of the model and the training technique, and (iv) the interpretability improves when dropout is applied.

(i) the interpretability of the latent representations of CNN models trained on different classification problems is highly dependent on the task, (ii) the interpretability increases with the depth of the model and is not an axis-independent property, and (iii) interpretability is not a property of the model itself, but is a result of training, and is affected by the training iterations, initialization, and the use of dropout and batch-normalization.
